meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's zero entered before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. I'm writing those times down. Did you speak to Owen before you entered that zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. I'll ask Owen for it. Whatever happens next, this stays quiet and off his record.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote from memory, or use a different edition. Is that your proof, one line?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I'll check the scene myself tonight. What else do you have, and what are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a finished essay, that's called revising. And you still haven't told me what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. To put this behind him, Owen will do the rewrite: private, replacing the zero, nothing on his record. I want that in writing tonight, and the rest goes in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. I'll confirm it with Owen tonight, and I'll want the time and room in your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, that its mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still want that in writing with the time and room, along with an answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, replacing the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants it in writing tonight with the time and room; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You showed her the quote on page two and told her to search the scene herself, because it gave her something she could check on her own rather than something she had to take on your word.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered, so it stayed open and went into her email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits close to midnight the night before the essay was due, came near that kind of night, and it proves nothing about the essay, which is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their argument between an outline and an essay, answer that with something checkable before moving on to the rewrite, since you went to procedure 4.4 with that point still open.
